newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher as Turkey row cools.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher as Turkey row cools.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on commercial buying with prospects for a resumption soon of wheat sales to Turkey cited, traders said.
"We figured it would be resolved, it was just a matter of time," a trader said.
A senior government agriculture official Friday said Turkey will set new ergot fungus limits for imported wheat that generally meet with U.S. export requirements.
Talk continued to circulate that Turkey next week will be in the market for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of wheat.
Support also came from firm French wheat prices.
That market's strength came on the heels of the firm close in CBOT wheat futures Thursday, the traders said.
Continental Grain was a key buyer of two million bushels of March and 1.5 million December, traders said. Cargill bought one million bushels of Dec, sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, below the 17,650 Thursday, according to the CBOT. Options volume was at 4,000, above 3,818 Thursday.
Wheat closed one to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 3-3/4 at $3.78-3/4.
In wheat options, Continental Grain sold 600 March $3.90 calls at 8-3/4 to nine cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 300 July $3.50 puts at 27-1/2 cents, traders said.
